fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure; Perimeter Fencing; Access Drive; Open Green Space
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clearance for emergency vehicles approaching the property.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure to keep a clear path around it for responders on foot.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Keep the rear access gate unlocked or secured with a breakaway latch to allow responders to reach the rear of the property without delay.
• Clear any vegetation or stored items from the walkway connecting the main residence to the detached structure so responders can move between buildings quickly.
• Post the property address visibly at the driveway entrance, especially if the main residence is set back from the road.
• Identify and communicate all access points to local fire and EMS so responders arriving from different directions know which entries lead to which parts of the property.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of parked vehicles along the path between the street and the main residence to allow emergency vehicles to stage close to the building.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Large Trees; Multiple Access Routes; Vegetation Along Driveway
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster to create gaps between individual trees and reduce how easily fire can move from tree to tree.
• Trim branches on large trees closest to the structure so branches do not extend directly over or touch the roof or walls.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants that sit directly against the base of the structure.
• Separate the ring of vegetation surrounding the structure by pulling back plants and shrubs to create open ground between them and the walls.
• Trim low branches on scattered trees across the property to reduce the ability of ground fire to climb into the tree canopy.
• Cut back vegetation growing along both sides of the driveway so branches do not hang over the travel path and vehicles can pass without contact.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from beneath large trees near the structure.
• Keep the ground beneath large trees clear of accumulated leaves, needles, and debris.
• Maintain open space between tree groupings so movement around the structure is not blocked.
• Keep both access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so emergency vehicles can reach the structure from either direction.
